A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EAIL research. Their complete main text, equations, six figures, five tables and supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EgoExo4D localization and action-recognition experiments, quantitative ablations in Tables 1–5, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the supplementary ablations in Table 5.

M1.justification: The two-stage alignment and localization procedure, encoders, reasoning modules, action-recognition component and losses remain unchanged. Vision-language guidance is emphasized more prominently in v2 but was already part of v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate localization and action recognition on the same EgoExo4D cooking subset: 173 participants, 60 kitchens, 564.13 hours and 35 action classes. Seen-room and unseen-room coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MnasNet, EfficientNet, IMUNet, RoNIN and NILoc+. Table 2 retains DeepConvLSTM, modified EVIMAE and IMU2CLIP. The supplementary CLIP, InternVL and SLIP comparisons are also unchanged; citation renumbering does not alter comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same splits, preprocessing, architectures, training schedules and metrics. Both use localization thresholds of 0.2/0.4/0.6 m, RS, and action top-1/top-5 accuracy. Supplementary evaluation settings also match.

E4.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same ablations of modality guidance, action loss, spatial/temporal reasoning, location attention, encoder choice, sequence length, residual connections and Stage 1 retrieval. The drift analysis and qualitative cases are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical result entries in Tables 1–5 match after equivalent decimal formatting, such as 89.6 becoming 89.60. Figures 4–6 retain the same curves, heatmaps and qualitative findings.

T1.justification: The localization problem definition in Section 3 and the losses in Equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both claim action-aware localization through hierarchical modality alignment, auxiliary action recognition and superior benchmark performance. The added emphasis on vision-language guidance restates an existing component; the shortened conclusion preserves the contributions' meaning and scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of action-environment correlations, drift reduction and ablation findings are retained. Section 6 preserves the same limitations concerning outdated maps, idle users and different sensor placements.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions and the project-page address are unchanged. The supplementary material already identified SLIP as the default encoder in v1; v2 adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 removes Konstantinidis et al., Privacy-preserving indoor localization on smartphones, formerly reference [30], and its introductory citation. The remaining cited works and substantive positioning against prior methods are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds 'with Vision-Language Guidance' to the title, expands the abstract and introduction to emphasize that guidance, and condenses the conclusion. It also adds a funding acknowledgement and renumbers the supplementary sections. Most prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives small sizing and spacing adjustments, including a larger EAIL block. Main-table decimal formatting is standardized, and the expanded title and prose cause modest layout reflow. Figures, table structures and displayed scientific content are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing vision-language training guidance explicit in the title, abstract and introduction, clarifying a dependency that v1 explained later. The shorter conclusion also improves concision. Removing one background citation slightly reduces attribution, but the method, experimental evidence, supplementary analyses and limitations remain intact; the overall gain is modest and primarily communicative.
